overview.heading: How the Restaurant Menu Maker works
paragraphs: Paste your menu the way you would write it on a notepad: one line per dish, with an optional description and a price. Enter the restaurant name and a tagline, choose a style and a paper size, and PiCraft lays the menu out as a one-page design.

Lines without a price become section headings, so you can group dishes under Starters, Mains and Desserts just by adding a line. Dish names are set prominently, descriptions smaller, and prices aligned consistently.
The model is told to keep every name, description and price exactly as you wrote it. You still have to read the result carefully, because a wrong price on a printed menu is expensive.

whatYouGet.title: Print PDF with bleed
whatYouGet.description: US Letter with 0.125 inch bleed or A4 with 3 mm bleed, at 300 DPI, ready to send to a printer.

whatYouGet.title: A print JPG
whatYouGet.description: The same print file as a JPG for services and shops that prefer images.

whatYouGet.title: A web image
whatYouGet.description: A 150 DPI JPG for your website, your Google Business Profile, social posts and delivery apps.

whatYouGet.title: Ten restaurant styles
whatYouGet.description: Bistro, modern, rustic, street food, fine dining, chalkboard, tropical café, Japanese zen, retro diner and wine bar.

whatYouGet.title: Your wording, kept as written
whatYouGet.description: Dish names, descriptions and prices are copied from your text, with section headings from lines that have no price.

useCases.title: Restaurants and cafés

useCases.title: Food trucks and pop-ups
useCases.description: Make a bold, simple menu for a stall or an event, with the street food style.

useCases.title: Bars and wine lists
useCases.description: Lay out a short drinks or wine list, one page at a time.

useCases.title: Delivery and online menus
useCases.description: Use the web image on your site or on a delivery platform page as a quick overview.

useCases.title: Catering and private events
useCases.description: Make a one-off menu for a dinner, a wedding or a company event.

tips.title: Write one dish per line
tips.description: Use a consistent pattern such as name – description – price, so the layout stays clean.

tips.title: Use a separator the same way every time
tips.description: An en dash or a vertical bar between name, description and price helps the model split the line.

tips.title: Add section headings as lines without prices
tips.description: "Starters", "Mains" and "Desserts" on their own lines become headings.

tips.title: Keep descriptions short
tips.description: Three to six words per dish. Long descriptions make the page crowded.

tips.title: Stay within about 14 lines
tips.description: More lines mean smaller type. For a longer menu, make one page per section, such as food and drinks.

tips.title: Include the currency symbol
tips.description: Type $14, €12 or 14 as you want it shown. The price appears exactly as written.

tips.title: Proofread every price
tips.description: Compare the generated menu with your price list line by line, and generate again if anything is wrong.

styleGuide.heading: Choosing a menu style
styleGuide.intro: The style sets the background, the type and the atmosphere of the menu.

items.title: Classic bistro
items.description: Warm, traditional and neat. Fits cafés, bistros and brasseries.

items.title: Modern minimal
items.description: Light, airy and simple. Fits contemporary restaurants and brunch spots.

items.title: Rustic farmhouse
items.description: Natural textures and warm tones. Fits farm-to-table and country restaurants.

items.title: Street food
items.description: Bold, casual and colorful. Fits food trucks, stalls and takeaways.

items.title: Fine dining
items.description: Elegant type and generous space. Fits tasting menus and upscale restaurants.

items.title: Chalkboard
items.description: A hand-lettered look on dark slate. Fits cafés, pubs and bakeries.

items.title: Tropical café
items.description: Leaves and bright color. Fits juice bars, beach cafés and brunch places.

items.title: Japanese zen
items.description: Calm and restrained. Fits sushi, ramen and Asian fusion restaurants.

items.title: Retro diner
items.description: Bold color and mid-century type. Fits diners, burger places and ice cream parlors.

items.title: Wine bar
items.description: Deep colors and refined type. Fits wine bars, tapas places and lounges.

checklist.heading: Before you print or publish the menu
items: Check every dish name, description and price against your master menu.
Check the spelling of ingredients, especially words in other languages.
Add any allergen information or notices that your local rules require, in your printer's editor or in a note on the page.
Choose the paper size that matches your printer: US Letter or A4.
Send the PDF with bleed to the printer, and ask for the correct trim size.
Print one test copy and read it under the lighting of your restaurant.
Update the web image on your website, Google Business Profile and delivery apps whenever prices change.

limits: A menu page holds about 14 lines. Longer menus need separate pages.
It does not add a logo or photos of dishes. The restaurant name is set as typography in the chosen style.
Local rules can require allergen and calorie information on menus. PiCraft does not add them for you.
The text is part of the image, so a price change means generating again.
Very small print can be hard to read. Keep each line short.
